reason: E2 mentions inverse Hall-Petch softening in ultra-nanocrystalline HEAs and low friction in UHV, but does not demonstrate wear reduction or link it to grain refinement under sliding. E1 states that fine grains and residual stress weaken the passive layer and reduce corrosion resistance, but does not address tribo-induced refinement or ion diffusion pathways. The key premise that sliding contact dynamically creates the nanocrystalline layer and that this simultaneously lowers wear while accelerating corrosion via defect-mediated diffusion is not directly supported by the cited evidence.
premises: Sliding contact induces severe plastic deformation and dynamic grain refinement (or amorphization) in HEAs
Ultra-nanocrystalline grain size leads to inverse Hall-Petch softening, lowering friction and wear
Fine grains and residual stress weaken the passive layer, reducing corrosion resistance
Increased grain boundary/defect density facilitates aggressive ion diffusion, destabilizing the passive film
The coupled tribo-corrosion response is governed by a trade-off between wear reduction and corrosion acceleration
